defuss-shadcn / Application / property-grid

Built with: CSS JS

Property GridATM

The inspector of every RAD tool: a two-column table - key, value - over one JSON object, dense by default. Nested objects and arrays become groups that fold; a click on a value edits it in place with an editor that fits its type (text, number, a switch, a select of options, a color, a date, a textarea), or with the one getEditorFn returns. keyRenderFn and valueRenderFn draw the cells. The JSON object IS the state: every committed edit replaces it in el.store and fires property-grid-change.

Native basis

A <table> - <th scope="row"> keys, <td> values - generated from a JSON object; the editors are the library's own .input, .select, .switch and .textarea, or native color / date inputs.

§A service's settings

Click a value (or Tab to it and press Enter / F2): text, numbers, a switch for booleans, a select for the region (sourceConfig options), a color, a date, a textarea for multi-line text. Enter commits, Escape cancels, Tab commits and moves on. limits and tags fold.

×%

§Render functions

keyRenderFn(key, value, ctx) and valueRenderFn(value, key, ctx) are called for every row; each returns text or a node for its cell - or null for the default. ctx carries the path, depth, type, the key's config, the whole source and the grid.

§Badges, units, icons

Keys get a type glyph, booleans a badge, latencies a unit, dates a relative label - the values stay plain JSON underneath (edit one to see).

×%

§Custom editors

getEditorFn(key, value, ctx) picks the editor per key: return an element (an input or a select - its value is read back, a range or number input as a number), an object { el, getValue(), validate?(), focus?(), immediate? } for anything composite, null for the built-in editor or false to make the key read-only. Every committed change fires property-grid-beforechange (cancelable) and property-grid-change.

§A slider, a tag combobox, a guarded value

opacity edits with a slider; tags with the Combobox tag input (type to filter, Enter or a comma adds, × removes, new tags allowed) - cloned from a template, read back as an array; budget refuses values over 5000 through property-grid-beforechange. Ctrl / Cmd + Enter or a click outside commits the tags; the log lists every change.

×%

§Validation

A refused value keeps its editor open, marks it aria-invalid and says why under it (announced). Rules live in sourceConfig - required, min / max, integer, minLength / maxLength, pattern, minItems / maxItems, with an optional message - and validateFn(key, value, ctx) checks anything else, across keys too (ctx.source).

§Rules and a cross-field check

Try port 80 (below 1024), replicas 2.5 (not whole), an empty name, an e-mail without @, or a budget above the limit (validateFn reads ctx.source.limit). The message shows under the editor until the value is valid or you press Escape.

×%

§Data in, data out

The object is the grid's state, so it can be read and written from outside at any time: getSource() / getProperty() read copies, setSource() / setProperty() write (a write fires property-grid-change like an edit), and el.store.subscribe follows every change - here into a Code mockup that marks the lines that just changed.

§Read, write, follow

Edit a value or press the buttons: the JSON on the right follows the store (changed lines marked). Apply JSON replaces the whole object - invalid JSON is refused with the parser's message.

×%

§Inspector in a closable panel

The Studio pattern: select something, inspect it, edit it. Click a box or an arrow in the diagram - the Panel on the right shows its properties; edit the name, the meta, the tone or the shape and the diagram follows. The panel closes with its × tool (the canvas takes the room); the Inspector button toggles it (data-panel-toggle - its aria-expanded says whether the panel is open).

§Select, inspect, edit

diagram-activate feeds setSource(); property-grid-change writes back into the diagram and redraws it. The panel is closable (.panel-close) and the Inspector button toggles it ([data-panel-toggle]).

×%

§Variants

§Comfortable, sorted, read-only

data-variant=comfortable gives the rows room; data-sort=asc orders the keys (arrays keep their order); data-readonly shows without editing.

×%

§States

Named states via the shared State API, bound on each grid:

  • default - the table: every key and value of the source
  • editing - one value open in its editor (config.editing is its path, data-editing on the grid)

The config is { source, editing, collapsed } - the JSON object is part of the state, so el.store.subscribe sees every committed edit. The first example carries data-state-demo; bun run screenshots drives it via el.api.setState(name) and captures screenshots/{mode}/property-grid-{state}.png.

Machine contract - verified against property-grid.schema.json by bun run verify:

§CSS view file

/* -- Property Grid -------------------------------------------------------------
   Two columns over one JSON object - key, value - dense by default. Groups
   (nested objects / arrays) fold; a value edits in place. Every color, radius
   and font is the theme's. */
@layer components {
  :where(.property-grid, .property-grid *, .property-grid *::before, .property-grid *::after) {
    box-sizing: border-box;
  }
  .property-grid {
    --property-grid-key-width: 42%;
    --property-grid-row: 1.875rem;
    --property-grid-pad-x: 0.5rem;
    --property-grid-indent: 0.875rem;
    --property-grid-font: 0.8125rem;
    min-width: 0;
    overflow: auto;
    overscroll-behavior: contain;
    background: var(--card);
    color: var(--card-foreground);
    border: 1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius: var(--radius-md);
    font-size: var(--property-grid-font);
    line-height: 1.35;
    &[data-variant="comfortable"] {
      --property-grid-row: 2.375rem;
      --property-grid-pad-x: 0.75rem;
      --property-grid-indent: 1.125rem;
      --property-grid-font: 0.875rem;
    }
    /* inside a panel body (data-flush) the panel is the frame */
    &[data-frame="none"] {
      border: 0;
      border-radius: 0;
      background: transparent;
    }
  }
  .property-grid-table {
    inline-size: 100%;
    border-collapse: collapse;
    table-layout: fixed;
    & thead th {
      position: sticky;
      top: 0;
      z-index: 1;
      block-size: var(--property-grid-row);
      padding: 0 var(--property-grid-pad-x);
      background: var(--muted);
      color: var(--muted-foreground);
      border-block-end: 1px solid var(--border);
      font-size: 0.75em;
      font-weight: 600;
      letter-spacing: 0.04em;
      text-align: start;
      text-transform: uppercase;
    }
    & thead th.property-grid-key {
      inline-size: var(--property-grid-key-width);
      border-inline-end: 1px solid var(--border);
    }
    & tbody tr {
      block-size: var(--property-grid-row);
    }
    & tbody tr + tr > * {
      border-block-start: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--border) 70%, transparent);
    }
  }
  .property-grid-key {
    padding: 0 var(--property-grid-pad-x);
    padding-inline-start: calc(var(--property-grid-pad-x) + var(--depth, 0) * var(--property-grid-indent));
    border-inline-end: 1px solid var(--border);
    font-weight: 500;
    text-align: start;
    vertical-align: middle;
    overflow: hidden;
    text-overflow: ellipsis;
    white-space: nowrap;
  }
  .property-grid-label {
    overflow: hidden;
    text-overflow: ellipsis;
  }
  .property-grid-value {
    position: relative;
    padding: 0 var(--property-grid-pad-x);
    vertical-align: middle;
    overflow: hidden;
    text-overflow: ellipsis;

    cursor: text;

    border: 0;
    border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
    background: none;
    color: inherit;

  .property-grid-bool {

  }
